jobs.description:
The application window is expected to close on: 09/20/2026

Job posting may be removed earlier if the position is filled or if a sufficient number of applications are received
.

Meet the Team

Cisco Cloud Security Group is a leading provider of Cloud Security and DNS services, enabling the world to connect to the Internet with confidence on any device, anywhere, anytime.

Our approach is twofold; first Umbrella, our cloud-delivered security service, blocks advanced attacks including malware, botnets, and phishing threats, while our predictive intelligence engine uses machine learning to automate protection against newly-discovered threats before they can reach our customers. Today, we handle more than 80 billion daily Internet requests from 65 million+ users around the world. Our global network has proven reliability and adds no latency. We protect each and every one of our customers' devices globally without any hardware to install or software to maintain.

Working at Cisco Cloud Security group means being surrounded by passionate and creative people who are determined to disrupt the Internet security industry with innovative ideas, world-class research and unrivaled products and services. It's a place where the best ideas are quickly transformed into products, features, campaigns and company-wide practices, with nearly 100% year-over-year usage growth.

Your Impact

As Engineering Program Manager within Cisco Cloud Security organization, you will be working very closely with the Software Engineering team, supporting cloud products and deliverables. You bring an AI-first Technical Program Management lens to everything you do, embedding artificial intelligence, machine learning, and intelligent automation into how programs are planned, executed, and delivered.

Besides solid program delivery and technical skills, you have proven experience in problem solving, managing multiple projects simultaneously, a deep understanding of cloud product development, strong background in CI/CD development model, and delivery of complex large-scale software projects.

You thrive in a fast-paced and demanding environment. You have the ability to think creatively and critically, lead through intellect, and are willing to roll-up your sleeves when needed. In addition, you are able to partner across a wide variety of functions. You have strong internal drive, a tenacious spirit, good communication skills and a collaborative method of working

Key Responsibilities

Bring strong Technical Program Management expertise with an AI-first vision, pioneering the adoption of AI-driven tools, automation, and data-informed decision-making to accelerate program delivery and drive innovation across teams
Support, track and manage complex program execution, cross-functional coordination, and inter/intra team communications to deliver outstanding, high quality program outcomes
Track and maintain cross-functional dependencies/deliverables, work with other cross-functional groups within Cisco Security to manage dependencies and deliverables
Provide timely issue resolution and critical path management; and facilitate good communication.
Drive day-to day program activities to meet overall program objective
Be self-directed with the ability to review changes and weigh tradeoffs between engineering resources and operational improvements
Provide weekly updates and offer multiple levels of status across a wide spectrum of individual contributors to executive management
Drive an AI-first approach to program management, identifying and deploying AI/ML tools and intelligent automation to streamline planning, reporting, risk detection, and decision-making
Partner with engineering teams to plan and deliver AI/ML-powered features, demonstrating data-driven insights and predictive analytics to improve program velocity, quality, and outcomes

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's + 8 years, a Master’s degree + 6 years, or PhD + 3 years of complex program management (preferred in software cloud environments), using both agile and waterfall. Degree should be in Engineering, Computer Science or related technical field.
3+ years of experience applying AI/ML tools, GenAI assistants, and intelligent automation to program management.
3+ years of experience coordinating cross-functional projects, facilitating team meetings, and collaborating with geographically distributed teams.
Prior experience in Lean Enterprise / Agile / Kanban practices and supporting tools.
Experience with defect tracking applications like JIRA and business applications such as Word, Excel and Project.

Preferred Qualifications

Able to communicate well with cross-functional team members, be able to efficiently collaborate with and influence team members to achieve project goals, and contribute positively to the engineering community environment.
Ability to understand, discuss / communicate technical concepts, with both technical and non-technical individuals.
Ability to find opportunities to embed AI across the software delivery lifecycle.
Working knowledge of cloud and network security concepts and technologies such as SASE, Security Service Edge (SSE), Zero Trust, DNS-layer security, secure web gateway (SWG), and firewall/cloud-delivered security.
Familiarity with security compliance and certification frameworks (e.g., FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, GDPR) and experience supporting audit- or compliance-driven programs.
Experience delivering programs in a DevSecOps environment, integrating security controls and testing into CI/CD pipelines and the software development lifecycle
Awareness of AI/ML security and responsible-AI considerations, including model risk, data privacy, secure handling of sensitive data, and threat modeling for AI-enabled products.
Understanding of vulnerability management, incident response, and secure SDLC practices; ability to coordinate cross-functional security remediation efforts.
Relevant security certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, CompTIA Security+, or CISM are a plus.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager - Business Technology
jobs.description:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

Note: This position requires presence in our San Francisco or San Jose office location 4 days per week; Lambda's designated work from home day is currently Tuesday

Business Technology at Lambda builds and scales the internal systems that power our business. We partner across the company with Finance, GTM, Engineering, and People to implement tools, automate workflows, and ensure data flows securely and accurately. Our scope spans enterprise applications, integrations, data platform and analytics, compliance automation, and all things IT.

We are hiring an IT Technical Program Manager to run the programs that make this portfolio move. You will be the first dedicated program management hire in Business Technology, building our portfolio operating model from the ground up: intake, prioritization, delivery cadence, and change management discipline. Business Technology is delivering a business transformation with roughly ten new enterprise systems this year and a growing integration and data footprint. You will drive cross-functional programs from kickoff through go-live and hypercare, and be the connective tissue between our five pillars: Finance Systems, GTM Systems, Data Platform and Analytics, IT Operations, and People Technology.

This is a hands-on delivery role for someone who runs programs with rigor, communicates crisply to executives, and holds vendors, partners, and internal teams accountable to dates. You will personally carry our largest programs while building the lightweight structures that make every subsequent program faster.

What You'll Do

Program Delivery: Own end-to-end program management for major system implementations across ERP, procurement, EPM, HRIS, treasury, and identity, coordinating internal teams, implementation partners, and vendors from contract signature through cutover, hypercare, and stabilization.
Roadmap Operations: Run the Business Technology roadmap: maintain the portfolio plan, manage a unified intake and prioritization process, surface dependencies and resource conflicts across pillars, and keep the roadmap honest against team capacity.
Portfolio Governance: Stand up lightweight portfolio governance: stage gates proportionate to program risk, RAID and decision logs, and a portfolio health view that gives the COO and CFO real-time visibility across all five pillars.
SOX Program: Serve as the program manager for Business Technology's SOX ITGC readiness workstream: track control design and remediation milestones across in-scope systems (ERP, procurement, EPM, HRIS, identity), coordinate evidence requests with external auditors and advisors, and report readiness status against the design readiness deadline.
Program Cadence: Build and operate the operating rhythm: weekly status, steering committees, executive readouts, and escalation paths that resolve blockers in days.
Change Management: Design and operationalize formal change management for Business Technology systems, including release calendars, freeze windows, and evidence capture that satisfies ITGC requirements. Partner with our SOX and compliance programs so control design milestones are built into program plans rather than bolted on at the end.
Cutover & Go-Live: Drive cutover and go-live planning: UAT tracking, readiness reviews, hypercare exit criteria, and post-launch retrospectives that actually change how the next program runs.
Vendor & Partner Management: Manage implementation partner and vendor delivery: SOW milestones, burn tracking, change orders, and holding partners to committed outcomes.
Executive Communication: Communicate program status to COO, CFO, and Audit Committee audiences with clarity: what shipped, what slipped, why, and what we are doing about it.
AI-Enabled Program Operations: Continuously improve how Business Technology delivers: templates, playbooks, and tooling (Jira, Google Workspace, AI-assisted status collection and reporting) that reduce program overhead and make delivery faster.

You

Experience: 8+ years in technical program management, with at least 4 years running enterprise application or business systems programs (ERP, CRM, HCM, procurement, EPM, or data platform). You have carried at least two large implementations end to end as the program owner, including cutover and hypercare, ideally with a Big 4 or boutique implementation partner on the other side of the table.
Technical Fluency: Fluent enough in systems architecture, integrations, and data flows to challenge a technical plan, spot a hidden dependency, and know when an estimate is wrong.
Compliance & Controls: Have operated in a SOX or audit-facing environment and understand why change management, access controls, and evidence matter to a program plan. Experience working with external auditors is a strong plus.
Operating Rigor: Run a tight operating cadence by default. Your programs have a single source of truth, current RAID logs, and no surprises in steering.
Builder Orientation: Comfortable defining process from zero. You can take a team that runs on tribal knowledge and give it intake, prioritization, and delivery discipline without adding bureaucracy.
Communication: Communicate exceptionally well upward and sideways. You can compress a messy multi-workstream program into one slide a CFO trusts.
Adaptability: Comfortable with ambiguity and velocity. Priorities shift at a pre-IPO company, and you re-plan without drama.
Attitude: An enthusiastic, go-for-it attitude. When you see a program drifting, you can't help but grab it.

Nice to Have

Direct experience with our stack: NetSuite, Salesforce, Coupa, Workday, Pigment, Workato, Okta, Lumos, BigQuery.
Pre-IPO or IPO readiness program experience, including ITGC remediation or Audit Committee reporting.
Experience with enterprise AI governance: tool approval workflows, AI inventory management, or build-vs-buy frameworks for AI-native applications.
Experience using AI tooling to automate status collection, reporting, and program hygiene.
PMP, PgMP, or SAFe credentials (useful, not required; judgment beats certification).

Salary Range Information

The annual salary range for this position has been set based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description.

Founded in 2012, with 500+ employees, and growing fast
Our investors notably include TWG Global, US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Andra Capital, SGW, Andrej Karpathy, ARK Invest, Fincadia Advisors, G Squared, In-Q-Tel (IQT), KHK & Partners, NVIDIA, Pegatron, Supermicro, Wistron, Wiwynn, Gradient Ventures, Mercato Partners, SVB, 1517, and Crescent Cove

Description

About Us:

Active Security designs, develops, implements, and sustains advanced C5ISR and security solutions to enhance defense and mission capabilities, addressing threats across physical, electronic, cyber, and communications security for Mission Critical Commercial and U.S. Government clients. Our teams are essential in installing, programming, maintaining, and repairing these complex systems in high-security environments, ensuring compliance with codes, client specifications, and internal standards.

Summary

The qualified Project Manager will have experience leading integrated security projects within federal, DoD, and other U.S. Government environments, including data centers, sensitive and secure government facilities, SCIFs and controlled spaces, detention and correctional facilities, health care facilities on government installations, and other classified or controlled sites, with project values ranging from $100,000 to $3,000,000.

The role of Project Manager is to plan, execute, and finalize government projects in accordance with contract requirements, strict quality standards, deadlines, and budget, while maintaining the highest levels of safety, security compliance, and customer satisfaction. This includes acquiring resources and coordinating the efforts of team members, subcontractors, and vendors in order to deliver projects according to plan, budget, and contract.

The Project Manager defines the project's objectives, oversees quality control throughout its life cycle, and ensures compliance with federal acquisition requirements, government security protocols, and applicable codes and standards. The Project Manager works closely with the Program Management Office, the Executive Team, and government stakeholders, including Contracting Officers and Contracting Officer's Representatives, to ensure timely, compliant, and quality completion of the integration process, and to support strategies for the capture and acquisition of new government work.

Project Delivery & Controls

Direct and manage project development from beginning to end, in accordance with contract terms and delivery requirements.

Proactively manage changes in project scope, identify potential crises, and devise contingency plans.

Manage site access, badging, and clearance requirements for project personnel at government installations.

Communication & Stakeholder Management

TAIT partners with artists, brands, IP holders and place makers to bring culture-defining, never-before-seen experiences to life. With a legacy of innovation spanning over 45 years, TAIT has grown from pioneering in rock ‘n’ roll concert staging to setting the global standard for extraordinary live events and experiences through cutting-edge technology, precision engineering, and creative design. TAIT’s 20 global offices have developed iconic productions and experiences in over 30 countries, all seven continents, and even outer space for renowned performers, theme parks, exhibits, and venues across the globe, including partnerships with Taylor Swift, Cirque Du Soleil, Royal Opera House, Nike, NASA, Bloomberg, Google, Beyoncé, and The Olympics

Position Purpose

Project Managers (PMs) lead the planning, development, execution, monitoring, and delivery of projects from start to finish. They are responsible for managing the full project scope, budget, resources, and team to ensure successful project outcomes. Our Project Managers focus on delivering results aligned with our core philosophy: “Happy Client, Happy Team, At a Profit.”

In this role, PMs typically spend approximately 85% of their time managing active projects or supporting project bids, 10% contributing to organisational and departmental improvements, and 5% on continuing professional development.

To support successful project delivery and collaboration with clients and teams, travel may be required for up to 30% of the role.

jobs.title: Health, Safety, Environment and Security Manager
jobs.description:
Company Description

Every minute of every day, Smiths Detection’s threat detection and security screening technology helps to protect people and infrastructure, making the world a safer place.

Smiths Detection is a global leader in the development, manufacture and management of security and detection solutions designed to make the world a safer place. Our technology provides threat detection and screening solutions for customers in our key markets: aviation, ports and borders, defence, and urban security.

Our expertise spans 21 global offices, seven manufacturing sites and five R&D centres, with a global network of 3,000 dedicated colleagues contributing towards over 40 years at the frontline of advances in safety and security.

This results in careers built on variety and the opportunity to work on a range of state-of-the-art solutions, where you can develop your knowledge and experience every day.

Job Description

Engage appropriate stakeholders and program managers to ensure collaboration in development and full implementation of HSE policies and procedures to ensure regulatory and company-wide policy compliance.
Lead and embed a high performing HSE culture across our UK and Ireland operations.
Develop training and audit/inspection tools to support robust site HSE program. Support regional specific HSE processes and procedures in support of company-wide initiatives and direction.
Develop and implement plans, processes and procedures to ensure conformance with regulatory OSHA, ISO 14001 & OHSAS 45001 certifications and company requirements and initiatives at all UK and Europe sites
Support the UK HQ with ensuring it meets its EHS legislative requirements.
Perform the site security controller duties. Must have Security Clearance or the ability to obtain this.
Drive continuous improvement in HSE performance for the UK and Ireland operations.

Key Responsibilities:

Advise site management team on HSE compliance requirements for our manufacturing site and service repair shop. Provide leadership and subject matter expertise that ensures appropriate HSE systems are in place. Coach site teams to improve HSE performance and engagement.
Manage and track site HSE Key Performance Indicators and drive site continuous improvement toward goals. Support problem resolution and provide leadership and guidance for the Site.
Ensure the timely & accurate reporting and investigation of HSE performance data and incidents.
Drive proactive safety culture across the UK.
Instigate and review vetting submissions and associated documentation and advise on overseas travel requests.
Chair Key Security meeting on site.
Ensure that site specific environmental targets are analysed, met and challenged for improvement.
Support site execution of tactical initiatives in order to eliminate hazards and risks. Drive continuous HSE performance improvement.
Continuously assess HSE hazards and risks and assist where specific technical expertise is required to meet local regulations or company policies, procedures and programs.
Plan and direct HSE activities and programs; establish priority for project execution based upon site resources and cost of implementation.
Actively participate in the investigation of significant HSE incidents and ensure timely and complete implementation of corrective actions.
Lead external registration and surveillance audit schedules for ISO 14001 & OHSAS 18001 (45001) with selected certifying body or registrar.
Develop and deliver specific site focused HSE training and education.
Develop the managements understanding of HSE issues and their role in mitigation
Act as a key channel for ensuring timely communication of significant site activities and events.
Support field service-based staff if required on HSE topics.
Prepare monthly submission for Global Smiths Detection HSE monthly call including best practice. Analyse trends for improvement.
Support emergency preparedness and response planning
Operate the safety management system for site and support the site strategy execution.
Assist the Smiths Detection European sites where specific technical expertise is required to meet local regulations or company policies, procedures and programs.
Support and participate in Smiths Detection auditing and benchmarking programs.

Competencies and Abilities:

Results driven
Strong influencing, leadership and coaching ability
Effective decision making
Confidentiality
Clear communicator at all levels.
Ability to drive culture change in HSE

Planning and Decision Making:

Operate at a strategic level with responsibility for global HSE impact and direction
Make informed, risk-based decisions aligned with business and regulatory requirements
Prioritize HSE initiatives based on risk, cost, and operational impact.
Influence senior stakeholders to drive effective and timely decision making
Travel anticipated at 10%

Qualifications

Technical Knowledge and Skills:

Relevant degree or equivalent experience
5–8 years HSE experience in operational environments
Experience with ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 systems. Awareness of ISO 27001 and its application.
Strong leadership and influencing skills
Excellent communication and analytical ability
Previous experience with security regulations in a highly regulated global matrix organisation advantageous.
Possession of strong organisational skills
Demonstrated ability in leading change and improving HSE culture
Demonstrated leadership and vision in managing projects/initiatives in a matrix environment
Ability to delegate and manage multiple responsibilities effectively
Ability to challenge and debate issues of importance to the organisation with diplomacy
Fluent user of Microsoft Office Suite

Additional information

Join us and we’ll help build your career, with excellent training and opportunities for career growth across the business, both locally and globally. You’ll experience an inclusive environment, with strong leadership and a focus on safety and wellbeing. You’ll also have the flexibility to choose from a wide range of benefits to suit your lifestyle, offering you and your family support from a health and wellbeing, financial and lifestyle perspective.

Join us and work for a world-leader, with the benefits and training to reward your dedication and skills. Be part of a team where we are making the world a safer place.

We believe that different perspectives and backgrounds are what make a company flourish. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment regardless of color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, economic status, disability, age, or any other legally protected characteristics. We are proud to be an inclusive company with values grounded in equality and ethics, where we celebrate, support, and embrace diversity.
At no time during the hiring process will Smiths Detection, nor any of our recruitment partners ever request payment to enable participation – including, but not limited to, interviews or testing. Avoid fraudulent requests by applying jobs directly through our career’s website.

jobs.title: Security Analyst
jobs.description:
Meet Benevity

Benevity is the way the world does good, providing companies (and their employees) with technology to take social action on the issues they care about. Through giving, volunteering, grantmaking, employee resource groups and micro-actions, we help most of the Fortune 100 brands build better cultures and use their power for good. We’re also one of the first B Corporations in Canada, meaning we’re as committed to purpose as we are to profits. We have people working all over the world, including Canada, Spain, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States and more!

Benevity is looking for a Security Analyst to join our Information Security team in a generalist role spanning security operations, application security, and security enablement. In this position, you will own the triage and investigation of security alerts, partner with engineering teams to fix vulnerabilities, and help build resources that strengthen our overall defense. Working independently on day-to-day operations while collaborating with senior analysts, you will leverage AI tools to accelerate workflows while exploring AI-related product risks. We are seeking a curious, analytical, and continuous learner who thrives on solving puzzles and empowering others to build a safer digital world.

What You’ll Do

Triage, validate, and investigate alerts across core security tooling (EDR, SIEM, IDS/IPS, CSPM, MDR) to establish scope and determine escalation
Maintain clear documentation, write incident response playbooks, and participate in an on-call rotation
Conduct threat intelligence research and contribute to post-incident reviews to drive preventive control improvements
Analyze SAST, SCA, and DAST findings, providing engineering teams with actionable exploitation context for remediation
Assist with threat modeling and architectural reviews to catch security risks early in product design
Leverage AI tools for faster triage and investigation while practicing safe data handling and validating outputs
Identify AI-specific product risks, including prompt injection, insecure tool use, and third-party model exposure
Track vulnerability remediation lifecycles, monitor SLA compliance, and report on recurring security patterns
Partner with engineering and fraud teams on joint investigations, security enablement content, and self-serve resources
Track and report on key security metrics, trends, and process developments

What You’ll Bring

3+ years of experience in security operations, information security, or a closely related technical role
Hands-on experience with security tooling across categories such as EDR, SIEM, CSPM, WAF, cloud-native logging, and SAST or SCA
Solid working knowledge of networking, operating systems, and cloud fundamentals
Practical experience using AI tooling in a technical context with a thoughtful view on its strengths and limitations
Scripting proficiency in Python, PowerShell, or Bash, paired with an interest in automating repetitive tasks
Familiarity with security frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK and NIST CSF
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a puzzle-solving mindset and a drive for verifiable answers
Clear, inclusive written and verbal communication skills, capable of translating technical concepts for non-specialists
A curious, continuous-learning approach and a collaborative desire to support teammates
Experience in SaaS, cloud-native, containerized, or API-driven environments, or relevant certifications (e.g., Security+, CySA+, GCIH)

Discover your purpose at work

We’re not employees, we’re Benevity-ites. From all locations, backgrounds and walks of life, who deserve more …

Innovative work. Growth opportunities. Caring co-workers. And a chance to do work that fills us with a sense of purpose.

If the idea of working on tech that helps people do good in the world lights you up ... If you want a career where you’re valued for who you are and challenged to see who you can become …

It’s time to join Benevity. We’re so excited to meet you.

Where We Work

At Benevity, we embrace a flexible hybrid approach to where we work that empowers our people in a way that supports great work, strong relationships, and personal well-being. For those located near one of our offices, while there’s no set requirement for in-office time, we do value the moments when coming together in person helps us build connection and collaboration. Whether it’s for onboarding, project work, or a chance to align and bond as a team, we trust our people to make thoughtful decisions about when showing up in person matters most.

Join a Company Where DEIB Isn’t a Buzzword

Diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging are part of Benevity’s DNA. You’ll see the impact of our massive investment in DEIB daily — from our well-supported employee resources groups to the exceptional diversity on our leadership and tech teams.

We know that diverse backgrounds, experiences, skills and passions are what move our business and our people forward, so we're committed to creating a culture of belonging with equal opportunities for everyone to shine.

That starts with a fair and accessible hiring process. If you want to feel seen, heard and celebrated, you belong at Benevity.

Candidates with disabilities who may require accommodations throughout the hiring or assessment process are encouraged to reach out to accommodations@benevity.com.

jobs.title: Enterprise Services Program Manager (ESPM) - 19439 - Roy Utah
jobs.description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

The Defense Systems CIDO PMO is seeking a Senior Chief Information and Data Office (CIDO) Program Manager (CIDO PM)
in support of Strategic Deterrent Systems Division (SDS Div) Functions in the Northern Utah area. Specifically, the ESPM will support Sentinel Program
. In supporting Sentinel the successful candidate will have responsibility to support all CIDO services to the program to include coordination of operations and maintenance contribution to the existing Digital EcoSystem and well as executing new projects to stand up capabilities on the Digital EcoSystem Roadmap. The CIDO PM will be the primary interface between the Sentinel Program Leadership and enterprise groups within CIDO Support team.

The CIDO leads all aspects of implementing innovative information technology (IT) solutions that deliver value and enable SDS Div/Sentinel Program strategic business initiatives. This includes leading all IT strategic planning and implementations, as well as day-to-day IT activity across the Sentinel program. In addition, the CIDO PM, in coordination with CIDO and Global Operations service lines is accountable for the delivery of all services that the CIDO provides, including Service Center Operations, Cyber Security, and Security.

Responsibilities will include but not be limited to the following:

Execute Chief Information and Data Office strategy and operational activities including service delivery, technical requirements gathering, build versus buy analysis, infrastructure solutions and project execution
Act as the CIDO ambassador to program leadership, functional organizations, and site employees and advocate to represent program requirements and concerns to the Defense Systems CIDO PMO management
Effectively interact with members of the CIDO, classified IT, and business leadership teams to optimize strategies to support goals and objectives, including managing budget and costs
Oversee proposal development, staffing plan development, product and service acquisition and delivery, teaming relationships and communication activities, thereby ensuring timely and cost-effective delivery and customer satisfaction
Coordinate testing and acceptance of CIDO initiatives, pre-production and support user training, and on-going feedback
Monitor customer satisfaction with service delivery and engage CIDO and Global Operations resources to assist as required to meet and exceed CIDO and Global Operations service level objectives
Develop strong/empowered relationships with cross functional sector groups. Drive and influence simplification improvements while understanding business partner/program business objectives and needs.
Escalate service actions and associated delivery priorities as required.
Identify systemic technical and service delivery challenges and then coordinate solutions with CIDO and Global Operations functional representatives; engage constructively to identify solutions
Develop, present, and obtain approvals for CIDO budgets, project plans, and functional/business unit initiatives
Deliver leadership, peer engagement, and highly effective collaboration across the Defense Systems CIDO PMO supporting Defense Systems sector, SDS Div and CIDO enterprise initiatives and project.   

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and 8 years of related experience or Master’s degree and 6 years of related experience
3 years of management experience/ program management experience
US Citizenship with Active U.S. Government Secret clearance with a reinvestigation date occurring in the last 6 years with the ability to obtain and maintain Top Secret clearance and SAP Access.
Must have experience in either project management, cost, budgets, or scheduling.
Must have familiarity with technical solutions, infrastructure implementations, process/project documentation, and/or liaison interfacing for large enterprise organizations.
Demonstrated ability to pro-actively identify issues and solutions to those issues, and drives issues rapidly to closure.
Excellent organizational, verbal, and written communications skills.
Ability to travel up to 10% of the time.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior Northrop Grumman Defense Sector SDS Div or Sentinel Program Specific experience.
Broad background in IT Infrastructure, business applications, and operations.
Ability to perform risk & opportunity analysis and prepare detail cost and technical proposals.
Active Top Secret security clearance with an adjudication or reinvestigation date within the past 5 years, and the ability to maintain the required clearance; additionally, the selected candidate will be required to obtain SAP access

CIDO

Primary Level Salary Range: $151,500.00 - $227,300.00

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. The selected candidate will be responsible for managing and executing comprehensive program security operations across multiple security disciplines, while building and maintaining effective working relationships with internal and external customers.

Serve as the program Security lead and assistant security manager to the customer, providing security oversight of all collateral and restricted program activities
Support a fast-paced, high-visibility program, providing proactive security guidance and solutions

Review and processing of documentation in support of DoD, SAP, and SCI nomination and adjudication processes

Accessing, reviewing, and submitting clearance/access information via DISS and other government systems
Maintain PERSEC databases in accordance with customer and corporate tracking requirements

Maintain and operate document control registers/databases; manage the receipt, transmission, reproduction, storage, tracking, and destruction of classified material
Process and manage incoming and outgoing visit authorizations; oversee visitor control procedures; coordinate with installation security
Maintain accountability of all classified material, including document registers, electronic media transfers, and secure destruction programs
Perform other security-related duties as assigned to support overall program and corporate security objectives
Other duties as assigned

Requires an active U.S. Government Secret security clearance at time of application, current and within scope, with the ability to obtain a U.S. Government Top-Security/Sensitive Compartmented Information security clearance within six months of hire
Must have knowledge and familiarity with the CFR 32 part 117 (NISPOM); Intelligence Community Directives (ICD); DoD Manuals, and other related security requirements
Excellent written and oral communication skills
Experience with Desktop Computer and Microsoft Office products
Ability to display tact, discretion, and diplomacy in dealing with all levels of employees and customers

Experience with DISS, SIMS, Lenel, or similar databases

Strong experience with risk management — identifying project-level risks early, building credible mitigation plans, quantifying risk exposure, and escalating only what genuinely requires SLT intervention with recommended options attached
SAFe or equivalent scaled Agile experience — familiarity with PI Planning, Project Increment objectives, ART-level ceremonies, and multi-team dependency management for Agile projects running at scale

Roles & Responsibilities

Own full accountability for project delivery across scope, schedule, budget, quality, and risk — from project initiation through delivery, go-live, and stabilization; the project's success or failure is this role's responsibility
Define the project roadmap and integrated delivery plan at the outset — break the project into logical phases or waves, identify the critical path, map all workstream dependencies, and establish milestones that stakeholders can hold the team to
Establish and operate project governance from day one — steering committee cadence, RAID log, change control board, decision log, and status reporting framework; governance must be operational before delivery teams begin work, not retrofitted after problems appear
Manage vendor and partner delivery organizations — own the SOW and contractual obligations, run regular governance reviews, enforce SLA commitments, escalate vendor performance issues through the right channels, and document all delivery decisions

Facilitate and own Agile project ceremonies where applicable — PI Planning, System Demos, Inspect and Adapt workshops — ensuring all teams have clear objectives, dependencies mapped, and capacity planned for each increment
Proactively manage the RAID log — identify risks before they become issues, assign owners, review mitigation progress weekly, and escalate items that exceed the project's risk tolerance with clear options and a recommended course of action
Lead change management activities — assess the organizational impact of the project, build a stakeholder communication plan, ensure business readiness activities (training, process change, cutover preparation) are tracked as project deliverables not afterthoughts

This position provides operational oversight to UC San Diego Health's Heart Transplant Program
.

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Defense Systems is seeking a Logistics Program Manager 2
. This position is located in Roy, UT
and supports the Sentinel Program. This role may offer a competitive relocation assistance package.

The selected candidate will be responsible for a Logistics and Systems Engineering discipline Section within the SDS Systems Engineering organization and will report directly to an SDS Systems Engineering Department Manager. You will provide career mentorship and operational support to a Functional Home Room (FHR) team (Section) of between 8 and 12 Individual Contributors (ICs) based on goals, objectives, and company policy. Key FHR responsibilities will be personnel performance management, process familiarization and training for Section members, as well as staffing of roles on projects.

As a Section Manager you will be expected to spend roughly 20% of your effort on Functional Homeroom responsibilities with 80% of your efforts focused on a technical assignment on an SDS project or IPT where the selected candidate will provide technical and administrative leadership and guidance to the Sentinel Business Units, Operating Units, and Suppliers. This includes managing a team comprised of both technical and program support personnel required to resolve technical issues, ensure compliance to both technical and contractual obligations, and ultimately to ensure compliance with the technical performance metrics (TPMs) documented within the contract Statement of Work (SOW) requirements.

The successful candidate will be experienced in systems engineering with one or more of the following specific skills: Model Based Systems Engineering (Cameo), Requirements Management (DOORS), Verification Planning, and Interface definition and planning.

What You’ll Get To Do

People leadership for a Sentinel logistics and systems engineering organization, to include performance management, career development, staffing, and merit planning.
Provide project and technical oversight for activities performed by the group.
Provide ownership of and direction to the processes used by the group.
Create a vision for an engineering and logistics team and work to make that vision a reality.
Provide proposal inputs and review proposal content for both internal and external customers.
Lead a diverse team of engineers performing project development, technical requirements review, system support, planning and sustainment for a diverse set of products in the missile, air and space domains.
Responsible for the strategic implementation of skills and labor mix; employee development; mentoring; communicating job expectations; planning, monitoring, appraising, and reviewing job contributions; planning and reviewing compensation actions; enforcing policies and procedures.
Interacts with senior internal and external personnel on significant technical matters requiring coordination between organizations to ensure successful task completion and customer satisfaction.
Responsibilities also include horizontal integration of best practices across the organization; maintaining cognizance over technical activities; and ensuring execution of project statement of work and baselines.
Excellent communication, mentoring, interpersonal skills, and the ability to collaborate with senior management, peers, and employees.
Provide ownership for the people, processes, and tools that support business areas and programs in achieving their missions.
Develop and adhere to budget baselines utilizing Earned Value Management (EVM) or similar cost & schedule control methodologies and tools
Identify risks and opportunities and coordinate with project teams to mitigate and retire risks
Ensure the program team understands and adheres to contract scope, and manages change through control board activities
Adhere to all internal processes, policies, and applicable industry standards
Deliver presentations to customers, executive management and other program stakeholders
Travel required to support supplier integration and test activities
Supporting FHR efforts in areas of process improvement, training and staffing

As a full-time employee of Northrop Grumman, you are eligible for our robust benefits package including

Medical, Dental & Vision coverage
Educational Assistance

Health & Wellness Resources
Employee Discounts

Bachelor’s Degree and at least 8 years of related experience; OR at least 6 Years of relevant experience with a master's degree or in lieu of degree an additional 4 years of related experience
Must be a US Citizen with an active U.S. Government Secret security clearance at time of application with an investigation completed within the last 6 years with ability to obtain Top Secret
Experienced in Systems Engineering processes, Logistics Engineering processes, and the 12 elements of Integrated Product Support

1+ years of experience providing technical leadership of a project
4+ years’ experience with ICBM weapon system logistics, operations, security, and subsystem integration.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a customer focused mindset.
Experience in the nuclear surety aspects of nuclear weapon systems
Experienced in all aspects of the engineering development lifecycle
Proficient with Teamcenter Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)
Demonstrate a track record as an effective communicator and problem solver who is able to develop and maintain good working relationships with internal and external stakeholders

Position Summary

This role owns execution on the strategic initiatives and projects most critical to the business. The focus is not on building program management infrastructure or managing a team of PMs. Instead, the Program Manager will take strategic priorities from concept to completion, working across the organization (Finance, Support, Enterprise, Partnerships, Product, and Operations) to improve how the business runs.

This role sits outside of, though closely adjacent to, our Product and Engineering organizations. The focus is on the operational and business side of the company, not product delivery. The Program Manager will partner closely with the Vice President, Operations, owning the operational follow-through on initiatives and projects.

Key/Specific Job Responsibilities

Own end-to-end execution of cross-functional strategic initiatives, for example (standardizing a handoff process between two teams, consolidating reporting across departments, redesigning a partner launch plan)
Drive projects across Finance, Support, Enterprise, Partnerships, and Operations, building alignment among stakeholders who do not report to this role
Build and maintain lightweight systems (trackers, automation, status reporting) that keep initiatives visible and on track, primarily through Asana

Translate high-level strategic goals into concrete project plans, milestones, and owners
Proactively surface risks, blockers, and decisions needed rather than waiting to be asked
Support the Vice President, Operations directly on prioritization, follow-up, and prep for key initiatives, roughly (10 to 20 percent) of the role, with the remainder focused on initiative ownership

Required Experience/ Competencies

A track record of driving cross-functional projects to completion without direct authority over the people involved

Excellent organizational and follow-through skills

Discretion and trust, given visibility into sensitive, high-priority work

Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

Approximately 5%

jobs.title: Network Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
Key Responsibilities

People Management & Team Development

Directly manage a team of Network Implementation Engineers across project delivery lifecycle; set clear performance expectations, conduct structured 1:1s, and own individual development plans.
Build a culture of execution discipline — ticket hygiene, change management compliance, documentation quality, and rigorous project close-out.
Identify skill gaps and build structured training and certification pathways aligned to ECI’s service portfolio.
Manage performance formally and informally; address issues directly, constructively, and on record when required.
Participate in hiring decisions for the implementation function, including technical assessments and structured panel interviews.

Project Delivery & Program Management

Own end-to-end delivery of network implementation projects spanning new client onboarding, infrastructure refreshes, office builds, and technology migrations.
Define and enforce project intake, scoping, scheduling, and resource allocation standards across the team.
Maintain active visibility across all open workstreams; surface and resolve blockers before they become client escalations.
Drive post-implementation reviews and root cause analysis; translate findings into repeatable process improvements for the team.
Coordinate with Client Services, Solutions Architecture, and pre-sales to align implementation timelines with client commitments and ECI delivery standards.

Technical Standards & Oversight

Serve as the technical authority for ECI’s implementation standards covering Cisco (Catalyst, Nexus, IOS-XE/XR), Palo Alto firewalls, Meraki, and SD-WAN platforms.
Review and approve low-level designs (LLDs) and implementation runbooks before execution.
Establish and enforce configuration standards that ensure consistency, repeatability, and alignment with client security and compliance requirements (SOC 2, PCI-DSS, NIST, HIPAA).
Serve as escalation point for complex in-flight technical issues; engage hands-on when warranted while ensuring the team learns from every resolution.
Champion Zero Trust and SASE architecture principles within ECI’s implementation workflows.

Client & Stakeholder Communication

Own implementation status communication to client stakeholders; translate technical risk into clear business impact language.
Represent the implementation team in internal delivery reviews, capacity planning, and service improvement forums.
Maintain ECI’s documentation standard across implementation plans, network diagrams, as-built records, and configuration baselines — ensuring clean handoffs to managed services teams.

Qualifications

Required

10+ years of progressive network engineering experience with a demonstrable track record in enterprise implementation, ideally within an MSP or multi-client environment.
3+ years of direct people management — you have hired engineers, set goals, handled performance, and actively developed talent.
Deep technical proficiency in Cisco networking (Catalyst, Nexus, IOS-XE/XR), Palo Alto firewalls (App-ID, Threat Prevention, VPN, Panorama), and wireless (WLC, Meraki MR/MS/MX).
Strong working knowledge of routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, EIGRP), VLANs, QoS, and IPv4/IPv6 fundamentals.
Proven ability to run multiple concurrent implementation projects with accountability for schedules, resources, and stakeholder communication.
Solid understanding of security frameworks, compliance standards, and change management governance in regulated client environments.

Preferred

Active CCNP, CCIE, or PCNSE certification; equivalent demonstrated expertise considered.
Experience with SD-WAN (Cisco Viptela, VeloCloud) and SASE / Zero Trust architecture in client deployments.
Familiarity with automation tooling (Python, Ansible) to drive repeatability and reduce manual effort across the team.
Experience with network monitoring platforms (SolarWinds, PRTG, Meraki Insights) and using telemetry data to drive delivery quality.
Hedge fund, financial services, or similarly regulated client-facing environment experience is a strong plus.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field — or equivalent professional experience.

Who We Are Looking For

Beyond credentials, we are hiring for a specific leadership profile. The right candidate:

Communicates expectations without ambiguity and follows through consistently. Leads with clarity.
Engineers respect them because they know the stack — not just the title. Commands technical credibility.
Holds the team and themselves to high execution standards without micromanaging. Drives accountability.
Focused on delivery quality and reliability, not just activity volume. Solves for client outcomes.
Understands the job is to build the best team — not to be the best individual engineer on it. Scales through people.

ECI’s culture is all about connection -
connection with our clients, our technology and most importantly with each other. In addition to working with an amazing team around the world, ECI also offers a competitive compensation package and the range for this role is a maximum of $142,000 annually with flexible PTO, health benefit eligibility the first of the month, life insurance, pet insurance, 401K and so much more! If you believe you’d be a great fit and are ready for your best job ever, we’d like to hear from you!!

Position Overview
SMX Services & Consulting, Inc. is recruiting a Contract/Project Manager (C/PM)
in anticipation of award of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's NSPIRE NextGen contract.

The C/PM is designated Key Personnel
and will be responsible for the performance of contract work and deliverables in accordance with the agreed schedule. The individual will have authority to act on matters relating to the daily operation and technical aspects of the contract.
This position is contingent upon contract award.

Mandatory Requirements
MUST BE A U.S. CITIZEN.

Must be eligible to work as a W-2 employee of SMX Services & Consulting, Inc.
for contract performance.
Must be able to satisfy HUD personnel security and access requirements applicable to the position.
Must possess sufficient technical knowledge to receive assignments, guidance, and direction from the HUD Contracting Officer and Contracting Officer's Representative (COR).
Must be available to support the contract's required operating schedule and project activities.
Must be capable of managing a complex federal technology modernization program.
Must be able to effectively manage communications with government stakeholders and technical/business teams.

Key Responsibilities
Serve as the primary Contract/Project Manager for NSPIRE NextGen.
Assume responsibility for successful performance of contract work and deliverables.
Manage day-to-day contract and project execution.
Maintain responsibility for scope, schedule, performance, and budget coordination.
Serve as a primary interface with the HUD COR, Contracting Officer, and other designated HUD stakeholders.
Coordinate cross-functional technical and business activities.
Manage processes, objectives, schedules, and deliverables supporting successful NSPIRE NextGen implementation.
Receive and execute assignments, guidance, and direction from authorized HUD officials.
Monitor project status and communicate risks, dependencies, issues, and corrective actions.
Participate in required program and technical meetings.
Support Change Control Board activities.
Participate in daily and integrated Scrum activities.
Participate in IT and business status meetings.
Coordinate preparation of required meeting agendas, minutes, action items, and follow-up activities.
Support disciplined Agile program execution and delivery.
Coordinate activities associated with modernization, data migration, security, testing, deployment, and production support.

Desired Professional Qualifications
Strong candidates should demonstrate experience managing complex federal or public-sector technology programs involving one or more of the following:
Enterprise application modernization
Cloud-based systems
COTS/XaaS implementations
Large-scale data migration and transformation
Agile/SAFe delivery environments
DevSecOps
System integration and APIs
Cybersecurity and federal compliance
Production implementation and operational support
Multi-team or multi-vendor programs

PMP certification is highly desirable.

Experience working in SAFe environments and/or holding SAFe Scrum Master certification
is also highly desirable because the NSPIRE NextGen program requires professional certification capability in these areas.

Security and Suitability
MUST BE A U.S. CITIZEN.

This position does not currently identify a Secret, Top Secret, or TS/SCI clearance requirement
in the solicitation materials reviewed.

The selected individual must, however, be capable of satisfying applicable HUD personnel security requirements. Depending on system access, requirements may include:
HUD-acceptable Personal Identity Verification (PIV)
Background investigation
Fingerprinting/FBI criminal-history check
Compliance with HUD information-security and access-control procedures

Continued employment on the program is subject to successful completion and maintenance of applicable government suitability and access requirements.

Employment Requirement
The Contract/Project Manager is designated Key Personnel
under the PWS.
For contract performance, the C/PM must be an employee of the prime Contractor
. This role therefore will be filled as an SMX W-2 position
, subject to contract award and final onboarding requirements.

Compensation
Anticipated W-2 compensation:
$77.74–$82.32 per hour

Equivalent annualized compensation at 2,080 hours:
Approximately $161,700–$171,200 per year

Final compensation will depend on qualifications, experience, certifications, contract requirements, and award.

Work Schedule
The anticipated contract operating schedule is:
Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM Eastern Time
, excluding federal holidays, with work performed in accordance with contract requirements.
Important Notice

This is a contingent position
associated with SMX's pursuit of the HUD NSPIRE NextGen contract. Employment and start date are contingent upon contract award, government approval where applicable, successful completion of SMX onboarding requirements, and satisfaction of applicable HUD security/suitability requirements.

What We Offer

Medical/Dental/Vision on the first of the month following hire
ESOP (Profit Sharing) and 401(k)
Paid vacations, paid holidays
Coverage under State Sick Leave
100% Prepaid College Tuition for employees and their dependents
Employee assistance program (EAP)

Additional Compensation Details

$112,600- $163,300K/ annually
Yearly review with possibility of increase based on performance and tenure

Job Description

The Enterprise Transformation Project Manager leads cross-functional initiatives that advance the organization’s strategic priorities, improve business performance, and strengthen the customer and employee experience. This role translates strategy into executable plans, aligns stakeholders around shared outcomes, and guides initiatives from discovery and business-case development through implementation, adoption, and benefits realization.

This highly visible role operates across business and technology functions, processes, people, data, and enabling capabilities. The position partners with executive sponsors, operational leaders, subject-matter experts, change champions, and external partners to simplify work, build organizational readiness, and deliver sustainable, measurable value. Technology may support some initiatives, but the role’s primary focus is business transformation and successful adoption.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities (
any combination of the following job duties)
:

Lead end-to-end delivery of enterprise transformation initiatives spanning operating models, business processes, organizational capabilities, customer experience, and enabling solutions.
Partner with executive sponsors and business leaders to define the case for change, desired outcomes, scope, success measures, and governance.
Maintain a tight working relationship across the business and technology leaders to drive forward strategic projects whether they are business-driven, technology-driven, or a combination of both.
Translate strategic priorities into transformation roadmaps, integrated work plans, milestones, resource requirements, and accountable ownership.
Facilitate current-state assessments, stakeholder interviews, workshops, and process mapping to identify root causes, opportunities, and dependencies.
Design and coordinate future-state processes, roles, decision rights, controls, and performance measures with cross-functional teams.
Build alignment across departments, resolve competing priorities, and support timely decisions through clear options, recommendations, and escalation paths.
Lead change-impact assessments and organizational readiness activities; partner with leaders on communications, training, engagement, and reinforcement plans.
Establish practical governance and facilitate kickoff meetings, working sessions, status reviews, steering committee updates, and post-implementation reviews.
Manage initiative scope, schedule, budget, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions, and changes while maintaining focus on strategic outcomes.
Define baselines, key performance indicators, and benefit measures; track adoption, operational results, and value realization after implementation.
Coordinate internal teams, external partners, and vendors, ensuring deliverables meet business requirements and support the intended transformation.
Provide concise, decision-oriented reporting on progress, financials, risks, outcomes, and actions to sponsors and stakeholders.
Embed continuous-improvement practices, capture lessons learned, and help business teams sustain new ways of working.
Coach employees and project participants in transformation, project management, problem-solving, and change leadership practices.
Ensure company policies, procedures, regulatory requirements, and internal controls are followed.
Travel occasionally to branches, operating locations, and conferences as needed.
All employees are responsible for food safety and are expected to notify the appropriate manager, supervisor, or key personnel if they witness any compromise to food safety or food quality.

Transformation Governance And Documentation

Own and maintain the transformation charter, business case, roadmap, governance materials, integrated plan, and close-out records.
Develop and own company standards for project management and other tools as needed.
Document current-state findings, future-state designs, business requirements, process changes, stakeholder impacts, and accountable owners.
Maintain risk, issue, dependency, change, assumption, and decision records with clear ownership, approvals, and traceability.
Ensure readiness, communications, training, testing, transition, and partner deliverables are reviewed and approved by appropriate business owners.
Establish benefits baselines and maintain adoption, performance, and value-realization reporting through stabilization and handoff.

Peripheral Duties

Support special assignments involving strategic analysis, business process improvement, operating-model design, integration, and enterprise change.

Qualifications

Desired Minimum Qualifications:

At least five years of experience leading cross-functional projects, transformation programs, operational improvement, organizational change, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into executable plans and deliver measurable business outcomes in a complex organization.
Experience with process analysis, facilitation, business-case development, governance, risk management, and benefits realization.
Strong change-leadership skills, including stakeholder assessment, communications, readiness, training, adoption, and reinforcement.
Excellent relationship-building, facilitation, influencing, negotiation, and executive communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, navigate ambiguity, resolve problems, and work independently with minimal supervision.
Strong analytical judgment and the ability to use data and performance measures to guide decisions.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.
Occasional travel may be required.
Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, organizational development, project management, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience considered.

Preferred Qualifications

PMP, CAPM, Agile, Prosci, Lean, Six Sigma, or comparable project, change, or continuous-improvement certification.
Experience supporting enterprise-wide transformation, operating-model redesign, business integration, or large-scale process improvement.
Experience in distribution, supply chain, food service, or another operationally complex environment.
Working knowledge of enterprise systems and data-enabled change, with the ability to partner effectively with technical specialists without serving as the technical owner.

Additional Information

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

All job offers for this position are contingent upon passing a criminal background check after a conditional offer of employment. No applicants will be disqualified based on the mere presence of criminal history, and an individualized assessment shall be conducted before any conditional offer of employment is revoked.

About The Team

At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We operate at the front line of real-world safety and risk management, translating user and operational signals into timely decisions, effective interventions, and improvements to our systems.

Within USRO, Risk Incubation & Systems builds the analytics, automation, monitoring, quality mechanisms, and operating systems that help teams identify risk, make sound decisions, and scale safely.

Our work spans emerging-risk detection, operational measurement, workflow automation, quality systems, launch readiness, and decision-support tools. We partner closely with operational teams as well as Product, Engineering, Data Science, Product Policy, Safety, Legal, and Support to identify high-leverage opportunities and build practical systems that improve outcomes.

About The Role

We are hiring a Technical Operations Analyst to solve ambiguous, high-impact operational problems using data, technical tools, and strong judgment. You will work as an experienced individual contributor across USRO, moving from problem definition through analysis, workflow design, implementation, measurement, and handoff.

The scope is intentionally broad and may span emerging-risk detection, operational quality, automation, launch readiness, and other priority programs. You will be expected to move between different problem areas as organizational needs evolve.

This is a hands-on role. You should be comfortable querying and validating data, building dashboards and lightweight automations, using AI tools to accelerate work, and working directly with operators and technical partners to turn incomplete information into practical systems.

Your work may also include data and operational monitoring issues for major cloud deployment partnerships—for example, validating pipelines and safety signals, investigating anomalies or discrepancies, improving reporting and escalation mechanisms, and documenting data limitations so partner teams can act with confidence.

Location / work model: London, UK; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.

Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. Strong discretion, judgment, and resilience are essential.

In This Role, You Will

Independently scope ambiguous operational problems and frontier & emerging risks, and turn them into clear analyses, workflows, tools, or decision systems.
Analyze large and complex datasets to identify patterns, data-quality gaps, operational blind spots, and source-of-truth issues.
Build and maintain dashboards, monitoring, alerts, recurring reporting, and workflow automations.
Develop systems for detecting and assessing emerging risks, including classifier, evaluation, labeling, and human-review feedback loops.
Support major cloud deployments and partnerships by validating data pipelines and safety signals, investigating anomalies, and improving operational monitoring, reporting, and escalation.
Design practical quality controls such as sampling plans, golden datasets, validation holdouts, thresholds, human review, and fallback paths.
Use AI and LLM-based tools to improve speed and scale while applying appropriate testing, quality assurance, and human oversight.
Translate technical and operational findings into clear recommendations, tradeoffs, decisions, and next steps for partner teams.

Document system logic, limitations, operating procedures, and maintenance expectations so others can run and improve the work.

Have 5+ years of experience in technical operations, data analytics, trust and safety, risk operations, product operations, or a related field.
Are strong in SQL and comfortable working with unfamiliar datasets, schemas, joins, denominators, and data-quality issues.
Have built practical dashboards, tools, automations, or operating systems and owned them from initial scoping through adoption and maintenance.
Can use AI and LLM tools to accelerate real workflows while independently validating outputs and managing failure modes.
Understand how to measure technical or operational systems using concepts such as precision, recall, coverage, error analysis, quality assurance, and human review.
Exercise sound judgment in scaled operations, including queues, escalations, reviewer workflows, capacity, quality, and incident response.
Move quickly in ambiguous environments, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and create structure without waiting for perfect requirements.
Communicate complex findings clearly to technical, operational, and leadership audiences and drive work through cross-functional partners.

Nice to Have

Experience in trust and safety, fraud, scaled or adversarial abuse, integrity, emerging-risk detection, or other high-stakes operational domains.
Experience supporting cloud, enterprise, or privacy-preserving deployments with constrained data access or specialized monitoring requirements.
Experience with classifiers, evaluations, golden datasets, labeling programs, reviewer calibration, or model-quality measurement.
Experience with Python, notebooks, data-pipeline troubleshooting, or other lightweight technical development.
Experience designing quality systems or workflows that involve vendors, BPOs, or distributed operational teams.

Job Description

Fusion Incident Management (FIM)

Department Overview

Fusion Incident Management (FIM) exists to reduce organizational risk and protect customers, colleagues, and the Bank by leading the coordinated response to significant fraud and information security incidents. FIM serves as the central command function that brings together fraud, security, technology, risk, investigative, legal, compliance, and other business partners to assess, contain, manage, communicate, and recover from high-impact incidents. The team provides a centralized enterprise incident management capability with 24x7x365 coverage, helping minimize operational, financial, regulatory, reputational, and customer impacts across the organization.

What you will do?

As a Senior Information Security Analyst within the Fraud Pillar of Fusion Incident Management, you will lead the coordination and management of complex fraud, financial crime, insider risk, and fraud-related cybersecurity incidents. You will play a critical role in protecting customers and the Bank by driving timely containment, recovery, investigation, and remediation activities while providing clear executive-level situational awareness and risk assessments. Your ability to remain calm under pressure, make informed decisions, and collaborate across diverse stakeholder groups will directly contribute to the Bank's operational resilience and fraud risk management objectives.

Job Details

Lead Fraud Incident Response:

Lead and coordinate enterprise response activities for significant fraud, financial crime, insider risk, and fraud-related cybersecurity incidents.
Drive containment, recovery, remediation, and closure activities while ensuring timely decision-making and action execution.
Track incident tasks, data, and workstreams.
Able to understand and ensure appropriate fraud detection, monitoring, prevention, and response controls are in place to address current and emerging fraud threats and fraud loss exposure.
Assess customer, financial, operational, regulatory, and reputational impacts throughout the incident lifecycle.
Provide incident leadership during on-call rotations and major incident events.

Enable Executive Decision-Making

Conduct incident severity assessments and provide risk-based recommendations to senior leadership.
Deliver concise, timely, and actionable updates to executives, stakeholders, and response teams.
Support crisis escalations and facilitate incident governance processes.
Maintain situational awareness and ensure stakeholders have the information required to make informed decisions.

Partner Across the Enterprise

Act as a central coordination point between fraud operations, cyber security teams, technology, investigations, legal, compliance, risk management, and business teams.
Drive alignment across multiple workstreams, ensuring accountability, transparency, and timely completion of response actions.
Provide subject matter expertise on fraud risk, fraud controls, investigative processes, and emerging fraud threats.
Build effective working relationships that support rapid and coordinated incident response.

Strengthen Fraud Risk Management

Evaluate the effectiveness of fraud detection, monitoring, prevention, and response controls during active incidents.
Identify risk exposures, control gaps, and emerging threats, recommending appropriate remediation activities.
Support regulatory reviews, audits, management responses, and control enhancement initiatives.
Contribute expertise to enterprise projects and strategic initiatives involving fraud and information security incident and risk management.

Drive Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement

Maintain accurate and comprehensive incident documentation as the single source of truth.
Support post-incident reviews, lessons learned activities, and root cause analysis efforts.
Identify opportunities to improve incident management processes, governance, and operational effectiveness.
